experiments.why: SVG with mixed case and a parameter must still be refused as inline-safe.
Active HTML markup with a charset parameter must not be inline-safe.
An external URL whose path merely contains the store prefix must not count as stored.
A served media URL with a query string must yield just the content-addressed file name.
A store URL with a traversal segment before a valid-looking name must give null.
A valid hash name behind a path separator must be refused by the name check or the dirname check.
A real 1x1 PNG data URL must be stored and named /api/media/<sha256>.png.
An SVG data URL with a charset parameter before ;base64 must be stored as .svg.
SVG markup declared as image/png must be sniffed and stored as .svg, not as an inline-safe .png.

source.quote: persists bytes to a content-addressed served URL

obligations.statement: persistMediaBytes(bytes, 'image/png') writes the bytes into the media store and returns a url of the form /api/media/<64 hex sha256>.png with a fileName ending in .png.

persistMediaBytes picks the stored extension from the MIME type: audio/mpeg gives .mp3, video/mp4 gives .mp4, application/pdf gives .pdf, application/json gives .json, and an unknown MIME such as x/y gives .bin.
persistDataUrl stores a base64 data:image/png URL and returns a url of the form /api/media/<64 hex sha256>.png.

source.quote: returns null for a non-data URL

obligations.statement: persistDataUrl returns null for a URL that is not a data: URL, such as https://example.com/x.png.

source.quote: still routes parameterized SVG data URLs through the markup path (stored as .svg, not inline-safe)

obligations.statement: A data:image/svg+xml URL, even with parameters such as ;charset=utf-8 before ;base64, is stored by persistDataUrl as an .svg file, never as an inline-safe type.

source.quote: else — notably `image/svg+xml`, `text/html`, and unknown/active types — is

obligations.statement: isInlineSafeMime returns false for image/svg+xml, text/html and unknown or active MIME types, so they are served as attachments rather than inline.
isStoredMediaUrl returns true for a URL that points at the store, such as /api/media/abc.png, and false for an external URL such as https://example.com/x.png.

source.quote: Extract the stored filename (`<sha256>.<ext>`) from a served media URL, else null.

obligations.statement: mediaFileNameFromUrl returns the stored <sha256>.<ext> filename for a served media URL and null for any other URL.
deleteMediaFile returns true after removing an existing stored file named by its content-addressed name, and the file can no longer be read.

source.quote: Validates the name + dir to defend against traversal.

obligations.statement: deleteMediaFile refuses a name that is not a strict content-addressed name, such as one containing ../ or a path separator, deleting nothing and not returning true.

source.quote: Delete stored media files not referenced by any live attachment.

obligations.statement: gcUnreferencedMedia deletes stored files past the grace window whose names are not in the referenced set, counts them in removed, and keeps files whose names are in it.
A pinned background file older than the grace window survives gcUnreferencedMedia even when the referenced set is empty.

source.quote: a satisfiable range yields `206 Partial Content` with

obligations.statement: For a stored file and a satisfiable single Range: bytes= header, handleMediaRouteRequest returns status 206 with a Content-Range header and only the requested byte slice as the body.

source.quote: yields `416`, and no range yields the full `200`.

obligations.statement: For a Range header outside the stored file's bytes, handleMediaRouteRequest returns status 416.

source.quote: no range yields the full `200`. `Accept-Ranges: bytes` is

obligations.statement: Without a Range header, handleMediaRouteRequest returns status 200 with the whole stored file as the body and an Accept-Ranges: bytes header.

obligations.statement: listMediaFiles never throws; when the media directory cannot be scanned it returns an empty list.
